prs.title: fix(shared): make McpError and UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe on v1.x
prs.author: NishchayMahor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Python's default `Exception.__reduce_ex__` reconstructs exceptions by calling `cls(*self.args)`, but `MCPError.__init__` stores only `error.message` (a plain string) via `super().__init__(error.message)`. clusters.pick_reason: #2703 is the only PR that fixes both the base class (`McpError.__reduce__` reconstructing from `self.error`) and the subclass (`UrlElicitationRequiredError.__reduce__`) in a single diff, using the standard `__reduce__` protocol for each. #2555 only adds `__reduce__` to `UrlElicitationRequiredError` and leaves `MCPError` itself still broken under pickle. #2478 introduces an indirect `_restore_mcp_error` dispatcher function but the visible diff does not add a `__reduce__` method to `MCPError`, leaving the base-class pickle path unclear; it also carries an unrelated `pragma: no cover` removal. #2703's inline comments precisely identify the crash site (`self.args` set to a bare message string) and the fix for each class independently, making the intent auditable.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2703: Python's default `Exception.__reduce_ex__` reconstructs exceptions by calling `cls(*self.args)`, but `MCPError.__init__` stores only `error.message` (a plain string) via `super().__init__(error.message)`. Unpickling therefore calls `MCPError(message_str)` or `UrlElicitationRequiredError(message_str)`, which crashes because both constructors expect typed objects (`ErrorData` / `elicitations`). All three PRs fix exactly this pickle round-trip failure in `src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py`.
